messages:
anya: noticed a perf regression on staging for long-prefill workloads with mixed-precision (4-bit + fp8) kernels. TTFT jumped hard on >2k token prefill.
kevin: ugh, when did this start?
anya: started rolling out with kernel-selector heuristic_v2 last night (deploy id: deploy/2026-11-03_02). Quick numbers: prefill TTFT for 2k tokens went from ~220ms to ~410ms on p4d-24. TPS also down ~18%.
matt: do you have a trace or profile?
anya: yup attached profiler snippet from perf-trace (shortened):
```
# prefill profile 2k tokens, mixed-quant path
kernel_selector: heuristic_v2
microbatch_size: 8
kv_cache_evictions: 3
cpu_sync_wait_ms: 12
matmul_fp8_ms: 85
matmul_int4_ms: 120
kv_fetch_ms: 90
other_ms: 90
TOTAL_PREFILL_MS: 420
```
kevin: looks like we picked an int4 matmul kernel for some attention layers but fp8 for others; the conversion/pack/unpack cost seems to dominate. Are we doing dequant/reqalign every layer?
anya: yes, selector switched some layers to int4 fallback because calibration score for those layers was marginal (score ~= 0.67). Calibration config used: `quant_calib=per_channel_mean_v2`.
sofia: can we repro with single-thread profiler run? maybe microbatching combined with KV fetch pattern causes cache thrash.
li: note that the KV cache eviction count = 3 per request — that smells like a boundary mismatch in the per-device KV shard size heuristic. If we evict mid-prefill we pay sequences of re-fetches.
matt: quick experiment plan: 1) force kernel_selector=legacy to see if perf regresses back 2) force all-attention fp8 path 3) run longctx with smaller microbatch sizes 4) capture kernel-level timings with nvprof.
kevin: I'll run 1 & 2 on staging (cannot change production). expecting legacy selector gives near-baseline.
ci-bot: build #3294 for kernel-selector-rollback passed; staging deploy queued.
anya: test 1 results (staging): legacy selector -> TTFT 230ms, TPS delta +15% vs heuristic_v2. So selector change is the trigger.
kevin: confirms selector picks int4 kernels for blocks with activation norms > 2.1 due to miscalibrated thresholds. We should not be choosing int4 for long-prefill sequences because dequant per layer is expensive relative to heavier gemm that stays fp8.
sofia: idea: selector should consider "prefill vs decode" mode — prefer fp8 on prefill for long contexts unless int4 gives >35% matmul speedup. Right now threshold is static per-layer.
li: also bumping KV shard threshold to avoid evictions during prefill would help. current threshold=0.6, try 0.8.
matt: I'll open a small RFC for selector change + new heuristic: add cost model that includes dequant overhead and KV eviction penalty. quick patch: https://git.redwood/infra/rt-kernel/+/PR-4277
anya: attached a short replay script to repro: `scripts/repro_long_prefill.sh` (uses 1k/2k/4k prompts and both selector modes).
kevin: rolling a canary with selector_v2-tweak (thresholds adjusted) to prod-canary. will monitor traces and SLI.
sofia: also raising question: our calibration pipeline reports per-layer accuracy but not the run-time conversion cost. we should add a calibration metric that estimates runtime overhead for mixed precision.
li: created ticket INF-1889 to add runtime-aware calibration + KV shard safety.
matt: for immediate mitigation, let's default long-prefill routes to fp8-only models. I can add a runtime flag `prefer_fp8_for_prefill=true` and short-circuit selector.
anya: That should be fine for now. Kevin, can you confirm canary metrics in 30m?
kevin: will do. if we see 95th TTFT drop back to baseline, we can promote.
ci-bot: canary deploy #3296 started.
kevin: Canary looks good so far: 2k prefill TTFT ~235ms, TPS back to +13% vs bad rollout. No new errors.
anya: awesome. next steps: 1) land PR to include dequant cost in selector cost model 2) add runtime pref for prefill 3) update calibration pipeline INF-1889 4) monitor longctx for one week.
sofia: assign me and matt on INF-1889.
li: i'll handle KV shard threshold change and a small test that injects synthetic KV eviction patterns.
matt: will follow up with PR link for the selector cost-model and perf numbers.
anya: thanks team. saved a bunch of perf headaches. :tada:
